title: Agarose Gel Electrophoresis
author: Alba Balletbó
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7zmhp46

steps.title: Prepare agarose solution
steps.instruction: Measure 1 g agarose (Thermo Fisher Catalog #75510019) and mix with 100 mL 0.5× TAE in a microwavable flask; TBE may be used instead if the same buffer will be used in the gel box. Adjust agarose mass for other percentages (e.g., 2 g in 100 mL gives a 2 % gel).

steps.title: Dissolve agarose by microwaving
steps.instruction: Microwave the mixture for 1–3 min until fully dissolved, avoiding overboiling; use 30‑45 s pulses with swirling between pulses, watch for boil‑over, and optionally cover with saran wrap. Handle the hot solution with care.

steps.title: Cool solution and add EtBr
steps.instruction: Allow the agarose solution to cool to ~50 °C (≈5 min, hand‑warm) then add 0.8 µL of 10 mg/mL ethidium bromide stock (G‑Biosciences Catalog #R034) and swirl to mix.

steps.title: Cast the agarose gel
steps.instruction: Place the well comb in the gel tray, then slowly pour the agarose into the tray to avoid bubbles; any bubbles can be displaced with a pipette tip.

steps.title: Solidify gel
steps.instruction: Let the gel set either at 4 °C for 10–15 min or at room temperature for 20–30 min until completely solidified.

steps.title: Prepare DNA samples with loading dye
steps.instruction: Add Gel Loading Dye, Purple (6X, no SDS) – 4.0 mL (New England Biolabs Catalog #B7025S) to each DNA sample; the dye provides visual tracking and glycerol increases sample density.

steps.title: Assemble gel box and add buffer
steps.instruction: Place the solidified gel into the electrophoresis unit, then fill the gel box with 0.5× TAE (or TBE) until the gel is covered, using the same buffer as in the gel.

steps.title: Load ladder and samples
steps.instruction: Load a molecular weight ladder into the first lane (e.g., 100 bp DNA Ladder – 500 lanes, New England Biolabs Catalog #N3231L or 1 kb DNA Ladder – 1,000 lanes, Catalog #N3232L) using positive pressure, keeping the pipette tip just above the well and withdrawing slowly; then load each prepared sample into subsequent wells following the same technique.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 80–150 V until the tracking dye front reaches ~75–80 % of the gel length; typical run time is 1–1.5 h depending on gel concentration and voltage.

steps.title: Stop run and remove gel
steps.instruction: Turn off the power, disconnect the electrodes, and carefully remove the gel from the box.

steps.title: Visualize DNA under UV
steps.instruction: Place the gel on a UV transilluminator, wear safety goggles, face shield, gloves, and lab coat; use long‑wavelength UV and minimal exposure if DNA will be purified later.

steps.title: Determine fragment sizes
steps.instruction: Compare sample band positions to the ladder in the first lane, using the manufacturer’s size markers to estimate fragment lengths.

steps.title: Excise desired DNA bands
steps.instruction: Using a sterilized razor blade, cut out the band of interest, minimizing surrounding gel; note that purification kits have limited gel capacity.

steps.title: Weigh gel slice
steps.instruction: Transfer the excised gel piece to a microcentrifuge tube and record its weight for downstream calculations.

steps.title: Purify DNA from gel
steps.instruction: Isolate DNA from the gel slice using a commercial gel purification kit (e.g., Macherey‑Nagel Gel and PCR Clean‑up Kit, Catalog #740609.250) or any preferred method.
